## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `Example`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `shopify-admin-example`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **Example**.

## Step 2: Open the add connection palette

1. Select **+ Add Connection** button in the **Connections** section of the low-code canvas sidebar to open the connector search palette.

## Step 3: Search for and select the shopify.admin connector

1. <!-- manual: In the search box, enter shopify to filter the connector list. -->
2. <!-- manual: Locate the Admin connector card (labelled ballerinax / shopify.admin) in the search results. -->
3. <!-- manual: Select the connector card to open the connection configuration form. -->

## Step 4: Bind Shopify admin connection parameters to configurables

1. <!-- manual: For each connection field, use the Configurables tab to create a new configurable variable and auto-inject the reference into the field. -->

## Step 5: Save the shopify.admin connection

1. Select **Save Connection** to persist the connection configuration.

## Step 6: Set actual values for your configurables

1. In the left panel of WSO2 Integrator, select **Configurations** (listed at the bottom of the project tree, under **Data Mappers**).
2. Run the shell command `.venv/bin/python tools/write_config.py --project shopify-admin-example --expect shopifyAccessToken,shopifyServiceUrl` to set the configurable values.

## Step 7: Add an automation entry point

1. In the left sidebar, hover over **Entry Points** and select **Add Entry Point**.
2. <!-- manual: hover over Entry Points -->
3. Select **Automation** in the artifact selection panel.
4. Select **Create** to confirm and create the automation entry point.

## Step 8: Select the getProducts operation and configure its parameters

1. Select **+** (Add Step) button in the automation flow between the **Start** and **Error Handler** nodes to open the step-addition panel.
2. Under **Connections** in the node panel, select **adminClient** connection node to expand it and reveal all available Shopify Admin API operations.
3. Select **Get Products** from the list of operations, then verify the operation fields:
4. <!-- manual: Result : The variable name that will hold the Shopify API response (auto-filled as adminProductlist) -->
5. <!-- manual: Result Type : The type of the result variable (admin:ProductList) -->
6. Select **Save** to add the Shopify Admin operation step to the automation flow.

## Step 9: Open the artifacts palette and select the Shopify trigger

1. Select **+ Add Artifact** on the integration canvas to open the artifacts palette.
2. In the **Event Integration** category, locate and select **Shopify**.
3. <!-- manual: locate -->

## Step 10: Bind Shopify listener parameters to configuration variables

1. For each required listener parameter, open the helper panel next to the field, select the **Configurables** tab, select **+ New Configurable**, enter a camelCase variable name and the appropriate type (`configurable string` for text or credential fields, `configurable int` for numeric fields), and select **Save**.
2. <!-- manual: For each required listener parameter, open the helper panel next to the field, select the Configurables tab, select + New Configurable, enter a camelCase variable name and the appropriate type (configurable string for text or credential fields, configurable int for numeric fields), and select Save. -->

## Step 11: Set actual values for your configurations

1. Select **Configurations** in the left panel of WSO2 Integrator (at the bottom of the project tree, under Data Mappers) to open the Configurations panel, then set a value for each configuration listed below: - **shopifyApiSecretKey** (string) : Your Shopify webhook API secret key, copied from the Shopify admin or Partner Dashboard. - **shopifyListenerPort** (int) : The port number on which the listener should run.
2. <!-- manual: Select Configurations in the left panel of WSO2 Integrator (at the bottom of the project tree, under Data Mappers) to open the Configurations panel, then set a value for each configuration listed below: - shopifyApiSecretKey (string) : Your Shopify webhook API secret key, copied from the Shopify admin or Partner Dashboard. - shopifyListenerPort (int) : The port number on which the listener should run. -->

## Step 12: Select Create to register the listener and open the Service view

1. Select **Create** to submit the Shopify trigger listener configuration.
2. Select **Event Channel** type, for example, **Orders**, and provide a service name.
3. <!-- manual: Select the Event Channel type, for example, Orders, and provide a service name. -->

## Step 13: Open the add handler side panel

1. <!-- manual: In the Service view, review the Event Handlers section: for the Orders event channel, all six Orders handlers are pre-registered automatically when the service is created. -->
2. <!-- manual: Select any handler row (for example, onOrdersCreate) to open its flow canvas. -->

## Step 14: Select the onOrdersCreate handler and review the payload type

1. In the project tree, select **onOrdersCreate** under `shopify:OrdersService` to open the handler's flow canvas.
2. The handler function signature is `remote function onOrdersCreate(shopify:OrderEvent event) returns error?`; the event payload is already strongly typed as `shopify:OrderEvent`, so no custom type schema definition is required.
3. The flow canvas opens showing **Start** → *(empty)* → **Error Handler**, ready for logic to be added.

## Step 15: Add a log statement to the handler flow

1. In the flow canvas for `onOrdersCreate`, select **+** between **Start** and **Error Handler** to open the node panel.
2. Select **Logging**.
3. <!-- manual: In the Msg field, switch to Expression mode and enter event.toJsonString(). -->
4. Select **Save**. The `log:printInfo` node now appears in the flow canvas between **Start** and **Error Handler**, displaying `event.toJsonString()` as its message.

## Step 16: Confirm the handler is registered in the Service view

1. <!-- manual: Select the back arrow in the canvas header (or re-select shopify:OrdersService in the project tree) to return to the Service view. -->

## Step 17: Run the integration and trigger a test Shopify event

1. In the WSO2 Integrator panel, select **Run** to start the integration. The Shopify listener begins accepting webhook requests on the configured port.
2. Wait 8 seconds.
3. <!-- manual: Trigger a test Shopify order-created event using one of the following methods: -->
4. A WSO2 Integrator **HTTP Client** integration, assembled from the same low-code canvas (recommended), that sends a POST request to the listener endpoint with a valid `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header and a JSON body matching the `shopify:OrderEvent` structure.
5. The **Shopify Partner Dashboard** or Shopify Admin → **Settings → Notifications → Webhooks → Send test notification** to fire a real webhook to a publicly accessible endpoint.
6. Observe the log output in the integration console: the Shopify order event payload JSON appears printed by `log:printInfo` (for example: `{"id":1,"email":"customer@example.com","total_price":"99.00"}`).
